mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes elastic behavior from plastic behavior of a material?

options.A: In elastic behavior, the material returns to its original shape after the load is removed; in plastic behavior, permanent deformation remains.
options.B: In elastic behavior, the material deforms permanently; in plastic behavior, it returns to its original shape after the load is removed.
options.C: Both elastic and plastic behaviors result in permanent deformation of the material.
options.D: Elastic behavior occurs only at temperatures above the melting point, while plastic behavior occurs at room temperature.

mcqs.answer: In elastic behavior, the material returns to its original shape after the load is removed; in plastic behavior, permanent deformation remains.
mcqs.explanation: Elastic behavior is reversible: when the applied force is removed the material regains its original dimensions. Plastic behavior is irreversible: the material retains a permanent change in shape after the load exceeds the yield point. Options B, C and D describe incorrect or unrelated characteristics.

mcqs.question: A block attached to an ideal spring is displaced 5 cm from its equilibrium position and released. Which statement about the restoring force acting on the block is correct?

options.A: The restoring force acts in the same direction as the displacement.
options.B: The magnitude of the restoring force is independent of the displacement.
options.C: The restoring force is proportional to the displacement and acts opposite to it.
options.D: The restoring force is proportional to the square of the displacement and acts opposite to it.

mcqs.answer: The restoring force is proportional to the displacement and acts opposite to it.
mcqs.explanation: For an ideal spring obeying Hooke's law, F = -kx; the force is directly proportional to the displacement (k is the spring constant) and the negative sign indicates it acts opposite to the displacement, trying to restore equilibrium. Option A gets the direction wrong, B ignores dependence on displacement, and D incorrectly uses a square relationship.

mcqs.question: What is the correct definition of elasticity in solids?

options.A: Elasticity is the property of a material to return to its original shape after the removal of deforming forces, provided the limit of proportionality is not exceeded.
options.B: Elasticity is the permanent change in shape of a material under any load.
options.C: Elasticity is the ability of a material to conduct electricity.
options.D: Elasticity is the measure of a material's density.

mcqs.answer: Elasticity is the property of a material to return to its original shape after the removal of deforming forces, provided the limit of proportionality is not exceeded.
mcqs.explanation: Elasticity refers to reversible deformation: when the applied stress is within the elastic limit, the material regains its original dimensions after the stress is removed. Options B, C, and D describe unrelated concepts.

mcqs.question: How is plasticity defined for a solid material?

options.A: Plasticity is the property of a material to undergo permanent deformation without rupture when the applied stress exceeds its yield strength.
options.B: Plasticity is the ability of a material to return to its original shape after removal of load.
options.C: Plasticity is the measure of thermal conductivity of a material.
options.D: Plasticity is the property of a material to resist any deformation.

mcqs.answer: Plasticity is the property of a material to undergo permanent deformation without rupture when the applied stress exceeds its yield strength.
mcqs.explanation: When stress surpasses the yield point, the material deforms permanently; this irreversible deformation characterises plasticity. Option B describes elasticity, while C and D are unrelated.

mcqs.question: Deformation of a solid can be classified as elastic or plastic. Which statement correctly describes this classification?

options.A: Elastic deformation is reversible, while plastic deformation is irreversible.
options.B: Elastic deformation occurs only at high temperatures, plastic deformation only at low temperatures.
options.C: Both elastic and plastic deformations are always reversible.
options.D: Plastic deformation occurs only in liquids.

mcqs.answer: Elastic deformation is reversible, while plastic deformation is irreversible.
mcqs.explanation: Elastic deformation returns to the original shape when the load is removed; plastic deformation leaves a permanent change. Options B, C, and D are incorrect statements about temperature dependence, reversibility, and state of matter.

mcqs.question: A metal rod is stretched within its elastic limit and then the load is removed. In another case, a copper wire is stretched beyond its yield point and remains elongated after the load is removed. Which behavior corresponds to each case?

options.A: First case – elastic behavior; second case – plastic behavior.
options.B: First case – plastic behavior; second case – elastic behavior.

mcqs.answer: First case – elastic behavior; second case – plastic behavior.
mcqs.explanation: When the deformation is within the elastic limit, the material returns to its original shape (elastic). When the deformation exceeds the yield point, the change is permanent (plastic). Options B, C, and D misassign the behaviors.

mcqs.question: A simple pendulum is displaced to a small angle and released. Which statement about the restoring torque acting on the pendulum is true?

options.A: It is proportional to the sine of the displacement angle and acts to increase the displacement.
options.B: It is proportional to the displacement angle (for small angles) and acts opposite to the displacement, trying to bring the pendulum back to equilibrium.
options.C: It is independent of the displacement angle.
options.D: It acts in the same direction as the displacement, increasing the amplitude.

mcqs.answer: It is proportional to the displacement angle (for small angles) and acts opposite to the displacement, trying to bring the pendulum back to equilibrium.
mcqs.explanation: For small angles, sinθ ≈ θ, so the restoring torque τ = -mgLθ is proportional to the angle and directed opposite to the displacement, producing simple harmonic motion. Option A gets the direction wrong, C ignores dependence, D states the opposite effect.

mcqs.question: A rubber band is stretched to twice its original length and then released, after which it snaps back to its original length. Which definition best describes the property demonstrated by the rubber band?

options.A: Elasticity – the ability of a material to resume its original shape and size after the removal of deforming forces, provided the deformation is within the elastic limit.
options.B: Plasticity – the permanent deformation of a material after the removal of forces.
options.C: Viscosity – the resistance of a fluid to flow.
options.D: Brittleness – the tendency of a material to fracture without significant deformation.

mcqs.answer: Elasticity – the ability of a material to resume its original shape and size after the removal of deforming forces, provided the deformation is within the elastic limit.
mcqs.explanation: The rubber band returns to its original dimensions after the load is removed, illustrating elasticity. Plasticity would imply permanent stretch, viscosity relates to fluids, and brittleness refers to fracture without deformation. Hence option A correctly defines the observed behavior.
